entry: American pop rock band formed in [[Los Angeles]]. Its original members first came together as Kara's Flowers in February 1994, while in high school. Renamed Maroon 5 in 2001, the band released its first album under that name, *Songs About Jane* (2002), which peaked at number six on the Billboard 200. In 2005 the band won the [[Grammy Awards|Grammy Award]] for Best New Artist. Its single "One More Night" topped the Billboard Hot 100 for nine consecutive weeks. Maroon 5 has sold more than 135 million records.

French military officer and politician. Lafayette volunteered to join the Continental Army under [[George Washington]] in the American Revolutionary War and in 1781 commanded Continental Army troops at the decisive [[Siege of Yorktown]]. Back in France, he helped write the *Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen* with assistance from [[Thomas Jefferson]]. After the [[Storming of the Bastille|storming of the Bastille]], he was appointed commander-in-chief of France's National Guard. He was captured by Austrian troops and spent more than five years in prison. In 1824 he visited all 24 states as the nation's guest.

French writer, libertine and nobleman. Best known for libertine novels including *The 120 Days of Sodom* and *Justine*, Sade was imprisoned for sex crimes, blasphemy and pornography. Born into a noble family dating to the 13th century, he served as an officer in the [[Seven Years' War]]. A series of sex scandals led to his detention in prisons and insane asylums for most of his adult life, including an extended imprisonment from 1777 to 1790, during which he wrote several novels. During the [[French Revolution]] he became politically active, first as a constitutional monarchist and then as a radical republican, and narrowly escaped the guillotine during the [[Reign of Terror]]. The word *sadism* derives from characters in his fiction who take pleasure in inflicting pain on others. Andrea Dworkin and Roger Shattuck have criticized the rehabilitation of his reputation, arguing that it promotes violent pornography.

City in Morocco, the fourth-largest in the country and capital of the Marrakesh-Safi region. One of Morocco's four imperial cities, it was founded circa 1070 by Abu Bakr ibn Umar as the capital of the [[Almoravid dynasty]]. Its red walls, built by Ali ibn Yusuf in 1122–1123, gave the city its nickname, "Red City" or "Ochre City". Marrakesh regained importance as the capital of the Saadian dynasty in the early 16th century and became a cultural, religious and trading center for the [[Maghreb]]. In 1912 the French Protectorate was established, and T'hami El Glaoui became pasha of Marrakesh. The old medina, with the Jemaa el-Fnaa square and numerous souks, is a [[UNESCO]] World Heritage Site. Marrakesh is a major tourist destination and is served by Marrakesh Menara Airport and a railway linking it to [[Casablanca]].

American television sitcom (1987–1997). Created by Michael G. Moye and Ron Leavitt for the [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] network, it was the first primetime series broadcast on the new network. Set in [[Chicago]], it follows Al Bundy, a former high school football player turned shoe salesman, and his lazy wife Peggy and their children Kelly and Bud. Running 11 seasons and 259 episodes, it is one of the longest-running sitcoms in American television history. Its sexually charged humor and dysfunctional family contrasted with earlier family sitcoms, and critical reception was mixed. The theme song, "Love and Marriage," was performed by [[Frank Sinatra]].

American multinational confectionery, pet food and animal care company. Founded on June 23, 1911, it is headquartered in McLean, Virginia, and is entirely owned by the Mars family. Its confectionery brands include Snickers, Twix and M&M's, and its pet food brands include Pedigree and Whiskas. The company operates four subsidiaries: Snacking, Petcare, Food and Mars Edge, its life sciences division. In 2022 it had US$45 billion in annual sales, and [[Forbes]] ranked it the fourth-largest privately held company in the United States.

Roman god of war and guardian of agriculture. Son of [[Jupiter (god)|Jupiter]] and Juno, Mars was pre-eminent among the Roman army's military gods, and most of his festivals were held in March and October, the months that began and ended the seasons for campaigning and farming. Under Greek influence he was identified with [[Ares]], though his character differs: Mars represented military power as a means of securing peace and was the father of the Roman people. In Roman myth he fathered [[Romulus and Remus]] through his rape of Rhea Silvia. [[Augustus]] built a temple to Mars Ultor as a key feature of his new forum. Mars's love affair with [[Venus (mythology)|Venus]] symbolically reconciled two traditions of Rome's founding.

City in southern France (pop., 2023: 886,040), prefecture of the Bouches-du-Rhône department. Founded c. 600 BC by Greek settlers as Massalia, Marseille is the oldest city in France and has been a trading port since ancient times. Situated in [[Provence]] on the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]] coast, it is France's second-most populous city proper after [[Paris]]. Its metropolitan area had 1,917,728 inhabitants in 2023. Marseille remains the first French port and the second Mediterranean port, and its Old Port is where the manufacture of Marseille soap began some six centuries ago. The city was named European Capital of Culture in 2013 and has the most museums in France after Paris. Calanques National Park lies in its southeast.

[[Wetland]] dominated by herbaceous plants rather than by woody plants. Marshes often form at the edges of lakes and streams, where they are a transition between aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Their plants are typically grasses, rushes or reeds, and many have aerenchyma, channels that carry air from the leaves to the roots. Marshes are distinguished from [[Swamp|swamps]], which are dominated by trees, and from [[Bog|bogs]], where acidic [[Peat|peat]] accumulates. The three main types are salt marshes, freshwater tidal marshes and freshwater marshes. Marshes provide habitat for many [[Invertebrate|invertebrates]], [[Fish|fish]], [[Amphibian|amphibians]] and waterfowl, and they filter pollutants and absorb floodwater. They contain 0.1% of global sequestered terrestrial carbon, but most natural marshlands are expected to be threatened by sea level rise and erosion.

Archipelagic country in [[Oceania]], north of the equator in the western [[Pacific Ocean]]. The country consists of 29 coral [[Atoll|atolls]] and five main islands, and 98.47% of its territory is lagoon waters. Its capital, Majuro, is home to approximately half the population. Austronesian settlers arrived as early as the 2nd millennium BC. The German Empire annexed the islands as a protectorate in 1885, and the [[Empire of Japan]] occupied them during World War I. The [[United States]] administered the islands after World War II and conducted 67 nuclear tests at [[Bikini Atoll]] and Enewetak Atoll between 1946 and 1958. The Marshall Islands is a presidential parliamentary republic in free association with the United States and joined the [[United Nations]] in 1991. The [[United States dollar|U.S. dollar]] is the currency, and the economy relies on U.S. aid, services, fishing and agriculture.

Canadian philosopher and media theorist. Raised in [[Winnipeg]], McLuhan studied at the University of Manitoba and at the [[University of Cambridge]] before beginning a career as a professor of English at several universities in the United States and Canada. In 1946 he moved to the [[University of Toronto]], where he remained for the rest of his life. Known as "the father of media studies," he coined the phrase "the medium is the message" in *Understanding Media: The Extensions of Man* and the term "global village." He predicted the [[World Wide Web]] almost 30 years before it was invented. His influence waned in the early 1970s, but interest in his work was renewed with the arrival of the Internet.

Infraclass of [[Mammal|mammals]] whose young are nurtured in a pouch. Marsupials are born in a relatively undeveloped state and nurtured within the mother's pouch on her abdomen. The group includes [[Kangaroo|kangaroos]], [[Koala|koalas]], [[Opossum|opossums]], [[Tasmanian devil|Tasmanian devils]] and [[Wombat|wombats]]. Of the 334 extant species, close to 70% live on the Australian continent, including Tasmania and New Guinea. The rest are found in the [[Americas]], where the Virginia opossum is the only species north of Mexico. Marsupials split from placentals 125–160 million years ago. Sizes range from a few grams in the long-tailed planigale to several tons in the extinct Diprotodon. The name comes from Latin *marsupium*, from Greek *mársippos*, meaning "pouch." Many marsupials have between 40 and 50 teeth, more than most placentals.

Brazilian women's football forward and national team captain. Regarded by many as the greatest female footballer of all time, she has been named [[FIFA]] World Player of the Year six times. As of 2025 she was Brazil's all-time top scorer, with 122 goals, and she holds the record for most goals in the [[FIFA Women's World Cup|Women's World Cup]], with 17. She was the first footballer of any gender to score at five World Cups. She won the Golden Ball and Golden Boot at the 2007 Women's World Cup after leading Brazil to the final. She was part of the Brazilian teams that won silver medals at the 2004, 2008 and 2024 Summer Olympics. At club level she won the [[UEFA]] Women's Cup with Umeå IK in 2004 and won seven Swedish league championships. In Brazil she is nicknamed *Rainha* ("Queen").

Weasel-like mammal in the genus *Martes*, family [[Mustelidae]]. The genus comprises eight species found across the Northern Hemisphere, in [[Taiga|taiga]], coniferous and northern deciduous forests. Martens have bushy tails and large paws with partially retractile claws, and their fur, which ranges from yellowish to dark brown, has been valued in the [[Fur trade|fur trade]]. The genus first evolved up to seven million years ago during the [[Miocene]] epoch. Martens are solitary, meeting only to breed in late spring or early summer. Litters of up to five blind, nearly hairless kits are born in early spring. Martens are omnivorous, and where stone and pine martens occur together, they segregate spatially because of differences in food preference, cold tolerance and predator avoidance.

American modern dancer, teacher and choreographer. Born in Allegheny City, later part of [[Pittsburgh]], Graham created the Graham technique, which pioneered the principle of "contraction and release," derived from a stylized conception of breathing. She established the Martha Graham Center of Contemporary Dance in [[New York City]] in 1926 and danced and taught for over seventy years. She was the first dancer to perform at the [[White House]], and she received the Presidential Medal of Freedom with Distinction. In 1965 she became the first director of the Batsheva Dance Company in Israel, founded by her former student Bethsabée de Rothschild.

American businesswoman, writer and television personality. Founder of Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia, which focused on home and hospitality, she hosted the television programs *Martha Stewart Living* (1993–2004) and *The Martha Stewart Show* (2005–2012). She was convicted of felony charges related to the ImClone stock trading case and served five months in federal prison, released in March 2005. Her company returned to profitability in 2006. In 2023, at age 81, she became the oldest woman to appear on the cover of the *Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue*. In 2024 she was the subject of a [[Netflix]] documentary, *Martha*.

German [[Nazi Party]] official and private secretary to [[Adolf Hitler]]. Bormann headed the Nazi Party Chancellery and controlled access to Hitler. He joined the Nazi Party in 1927 and the [[Schutzstaffel|Schutzstaffel (SS)]] in 1937. After [[Rudolf Hess]] flew to Britain in 1941, Bormann took over Hess's duties. He likely died by suicide while fleeing Berlin in May 1945. He was convicted in absentia at the [[Nuremberg trials]] and sentenced to death. His remains were found in 1972, and DNA tests in 1998 confirmed their identity.

German philosopher central to [[Phenomenology (philosophy)|phenomenology]], hermeneutics and [[Existentialism|existentialism]]. His magnum opus, *Being and Time* (1927), introduced the concept of *Dasein* ("being-there") and reawakened what he called "the question of being," which he believed had been neglected in Western philosophy since the ancient Greeks. His later work turned to technology, language, art and poetry. Thinkers including [[Jean-Paul Sartre]], [[Hannah Arendt]], [[Jacques Derrida]] and [[Michel Foucault]] were substantially shaped by engagement with his thought. In April 1933 he was elected rector of the University of Freiburg and joined the [[Nazi Party]], a membership he kept until 1945. He was banned from teaching after the war, a ban lifted in 1949. His involvement with Nazism remains the subject of significant scholarly controversy.

American Baptist minister and civil rights leader. King led the [[Civil rights movement|civil rights movement]] from 1955 until his assassination in 1968, using nonviolence and sometimes civil disobedience against Jim Crow laws. He oversaw the 1955 Montgomery bus boycott and was the first president of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference. In 1963 he delivered his "[[I Have a Dream]]" speech at the March on Washington. The movement achieved legislative gains in the [[Civil Rights Act of 1964]], the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and the Fair Housing Act of 1968. King won the 1964 Nobel Peace Prize. In his final years he also opposed poverty and the Vietnam War. The FBI under J. Edgar Hoover treated him as a target of [[COINTELPRO]]. King was assassinated in [[Memphis, Tennessee]] on April 4, 1968; [[James Earl Ray]] was convicted of the killing, though conspiracy theories persist.

Irish playwright and filmmaker. Known for absurdist dark humor, McDonagh wrote the Leenane Trilogy, set in County Galway, which includes *The Beauty Queen of Leenane* (1996). His other plays include *The Lieutenant of Inishmore* (2001), *The Pillowman* (2003) and *Hangmen* (2015). He won an Academy Award for the short film *Six Shooter* (2004). He then wrote and directed the features *In Bruges* (2008), *Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri* (2017) and *The Banshees of Inisherin* (2022).

American film director, one of the major figures of the [[New Hollywood]] era. Scorsese's films often explore crime, machismo, nihilism and Catholic concepts of guilt and redemption. His trademark style, first shown in *Mean Streets* (1973), includes extensive slow motion, freeze frames and voice-over narration. He directed [[Robert De Niro]] in nine more films, including *Taxi Driver* (1976), *Raging Bull* (1980) and *Goodfellas* (1990). He later made six films with [[Leonardo DiCaprio]], including *The Departed* (2006), which won him the [[Academy Awards|Academy Award]] for Best Director. Scorsese also founded several nonprofit organizations, including The Film Foundation in 1990, to promote film preservation, and has made documentaries on rock music and film history.

American actor. Born Ramón Antonio Gerardo Estévez, he adopted the stage name Martin Sheen to help him gain acting parts. He was nominated for a Tony Award for *The Subject Was Roses* (1964) and gained recognition for *Badlands* (1973) and [[Francis Ford Coppola]]'s *Apocalypse Now* (1979). He played President Josiah "Jed" Bartlet in *The West Wing* (1999–2006), a role that earned him six Emmy nominations. He received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] in 1989. Sheen has been active in liberal politics, and all four of his children are actors.

American investor and businessman. Born in [[Brooklyn]], Shkreli co-founded several hedge funds, along with the pharmaceutical firms Retrophin and Turing Pharmaceuticals, which he led as chief executive. In 2015 Turing raised the price of the antiparasitic drug Daraprim from $13.50 to $750.00 per pill, a move that drew widespread criticism. In 2017 he was convicted of securities fraud and conspiracy and sentenced to seven years in prison. He was released early from federal prison in May 2022 and is permanently banned from serving as an officer of any publicly traded company.

Canadian comedian and actor. Known for sketch comedy on *SCTV* and [[Saturday Night Live]], he created the characters Jiminy Glick and Ed Grimley. He won a Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical for *Little Me* (1998–1999). His films include *Three Amigos* (1986) and *Father of the Bride* (1991). Short co-starred with [[Steve Martin]] and [[Selena Gomez]] in the Hulu series *Only Murders in the Building*. He was made an officer of the Order of Canada in 2019.

Eighth president of the United States, 1837–1841. Van Buren helped found the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] with [[Andrew Jackson]], whom he served as vice president from 1833 to 1837. His presidency was dominated by the Panic of 1837, and Congress delayed implementation of his Independent Treasury system until 1840. He lost his 1840 re-election bid to William Henry Harrison. His opposition to the annexation of [[Texas]] angered Southern Democrats, who nominated [[James K. Polk]] in 1844. In 1848 he ran as the Free Soil Party nominee. Historians often rank him as a below-average president, largely because of his handling of the Panic.
